q: He maun be a saft sap, wi' a head nae better than a fozy frosted turnip—it wad hae ta'en a hantle o' them to scaur Andrew Fairservice out o' his tale.
1817 December 31 (indicated as 1818), [Walter Scott], chapter I, in Rob Roy. […], volume II, Edinburgh: […] James Ballantyne and Co. for Archibald Constable and Co. […]; London: Longman, Hurst, Rees,

In years when grain was raw and light,
So fozy it would scarcely dight,
I look'd around me, left and right,
⁠As sharp's a razor,
Till I got some unskilful wight
⁠To buy by measure.
1847, Scoundrel Will's advice to his sons:
Just a plain, stout, fozy, sappy burrow-man, keeping a gospel shop, with scarcely so much of a man's parts as will let him fend a blow in the face.
